data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 treats the necessity of author/checker engine separation as a purely statistical matter, judging single-engine verification genuine if its false-claim rejection rate is 'statistically comparable' to a separate engine. But the problem statement supplies a specific reason separation matters — the SAME engine that authors a claim is 'often trusted to also check it' — i.e., the shared training-history correlation that makes an authoring engine's prior likely to be the sole determinant of its checking verdict. A within-run false-claim rejection rate cannot be measured from a single run, and SRC_001 never identifies within-run evidence that distinguishes a computed constraint from a prior-driven verdict. Its countercondition (engine prior shown to be sole determinant, no causal role for execution result) is the very defect the problem asks it to detect, but the target offers no within-run marker that would trigger it; the statistical-reliability frame silently assumes exactly the multi-run population baseline it admits is unavailable.
